bibliography.title: Solubility of molecular hydrogen in silicate melts and consequences for volatile evolution of terrestrial planets

hirschmann2012_supplement.inspection: Entire word/document.xml: Data Supplement; Compositions of starting materials and EMPA analyses of selected quenched glasses; Series 1 and Series 2 tables and footnotes. Cross-checked against main-paper Tables 1-2 and Fig. 4.
hirschmann2012_supplement.identity: Starting-material types and five exact experimental identifiers match the main paper. The supplied file contains no separate bibliographic cover.
hirschmann2012_supplement.content: Two starting compositions and six selected quenched-glass analyses. It is not a run-by-run composition table for all 30 experiments.
hirschmann2012_supplement.label_discrepancy: The supplement labels B808, whereas main-paper Tables 1-2 list A808. No equivalence or correction is assumed; that column is excluded from the matched-run calculation.
hirschmann2012_supplement.starting_material_note: Starting major elements are volatile-free. Basalt added volatiles differ among experiment groups: 1.4 wt% CH4; 4.8 wt% CH4 plus 0.2 wt% H2; or 2.95 wt% CH4 plus 0.12 wt% H2 plus 1.93 wt% H2O. These are preparation inputs, not measured dissolved amounts.

reconstruction_method.basis: A declared direct reconstruction using unrenormalized central EMPA oxide wt% and main-paper FTIR H2/H2O wt% on a common 100 g basis. This assumption does not establish the authors exact unpublished calculation.
reconstruction_method.uncertainty: Rounded central values only; no propagation of EMPA, FTIR, fugacity or absorption-calibration uncertainties. Missing compositions are not filled from the starting mix.

hirschmann2012_supplement.outcome: The oxide-plus-water denominator can now be constructed for five matched runs. Differences from printed ln K range from -0.091864 to +0.018066; exact reproduction is not established. The provider still counts dry MELTS endmembers rather than oxide components. No constants or runtime formulas were changed.
remaining: Unreported per-run composition/normalization details and exact Fig. 4 reconstruction
Provider concentration-basis choice and empirical application error

thompson2025_notebook.execution: Notebook parsed and selected source cells and saved outputs inspected; author fitting code was not executed and no posterior was refitted.

cell_locations_zero_based.3: Reads pooled CSV; XOH=OH_Conc_ppm/1e6; selects fH2O>0.
cell_locations_zero_based.8-9: Divides responses and oxide predictors by their means; input *_MF columns are used as supplied.
cell_locations_zero_based.51,55: Five-oxide model and all-five fit in CaO,SiO2,MgO,Al2O3,FeO order.
cell_locations_zero_based.104-105: Descaling formulas. Cell 105 saved output matches paper Table 4 after rounding; cell 104 is a separately sampled subset-model result.
cell_locations_zero_based.110-111: Final expression evaluates supplied dry oxide fractions without renormalizing the five fitted terms.

pooled_sossi_comparison.method: Compare the fresh combined CSV with the byte-pinned archived Sossi23_Data.csv. A fresh raw Sossi download is not asserted.
pooled_sossi_comparison.interpretation: All six retained oxide mole-fraction columns are identical across the 12 matching rows. The OH column uses one OH/H2O molar-mass factor. Literal two-OH-group counting would double this value; no author convention correction is inferred.

thompson2025_notebook.remaining: Response scaling and source parameters are confirmed; finite-water Gibbs continuation, atomic species mapping and high-pressure/wet-host empirical support remain separate questions.

bibliography.title: Primordial hydrogen partitioning at Earth’s core–mantle boundary: Multicomponent effects revealed by machine learning-augmented first-principles simulations

jiang2025.inspection: Full nine-page paper; Sections 2.1-2.4, Eqs. 4-8 (printed p.1004), Section 3.2, Table S1 and Data Availability (p.1008). Equations and Table S1 were visually inspected.
jiang2025.evidence_kind: DFT/ML thermodynamic-integration calculations; not new experimental measurements.
jiang2025.partition_convention: D_H=c_H_alloy/c_H_silicate, with c_H the H atomic concentration; not a mass-concentration ratio.
jiang2025.notation_gap: Section 2.4 writes x_H=x/(97-96x) for the grouped alloy formula, but later writes x_H=1/[1+(1/c_H)] while calling c_H an atomic percentage. These printed mappings are not adopted as interchangeable; a quantitative refit needs a consistent composition map.
jiang2025.raw_data: Table S1 is recovered. Data Availability states that raw datasets are available from the authors on request; those raw trajectories/training data were not obtained and no author was contacted.
jiang2025.provider_implication: This fixed-P/T composition path supplies a comparison target, not fitted H excess terms or an absolute H standard for MaFeSiOHLiquid. It does not validate the 2173.15 K, 1 bar M2 candidate.

nozaki1966.inspection: Image-only original PDF; visually inspected printed pp.1823,1829-1831: English synopsis, Section 4.4, Eqs.7/7a/7b, Table 6 and Figs.10-11.
nozaki1966.scope_correction: The historical ledger quoted the whole-paper English synopsis range 1450-1670 degC. Section 4.4 explicitly gives 1427-1610 degC for the Fe-P interaction coefficient. Table 6 includes higher-P points, but they do not extend the stated P<6 wt% linear approximation.
nozaki1966.provider_comparison: examples/m2_material/phosphorus_reference.py retains e_H_P=0.015, matching Eq.7a. The old ledger and pinned artifacts are preserved; this dated review adds the narrower source-specific scope without changing a runtime domain or fitting finite-P interactions.
